raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-mixed-chunk`, a prefill chunk carries the running requests' decode tokens at its end and the batch
runs as `EXTEND`. For DeepSeek-family MLA models on `trtllm_mla`, `handle_attention_trtllm_mla` sends every
non-speculative extend batch to `MHA_CHUNKED_KV`, so each one-token decode row is treated like a prefill request: its
whole cached context is up-projected through `kv_b_proj` and attended with the non-absorbed MHA, prefix chunk by
prefix chunk (`capacity // batch_size` tokens per request per chunk). A decode batch does the same work with one
absorbed MLA decode kernel over the latent cache. As a result, turning on mixed chunks makes decode slower: on
DeepSeek-V2-Lite (below) W3's TPOT is 7.6 ms without mixed chunks and 16.7 ms with them.

This is the MLA counterpart of #43238 (BF16 MHA decode tails on `trtllm_mha`). #30338 does the same split for the
DeepSeek-V4 backend.

Scope on current defaults: extend batches that fit the prefill CUDA graph (≤ 2048 tokens by default) already run
the absorbed MLA path inside the graph, so this changes only larger mixed batches, which is the common case with
`--chunked-prefill-size` 8k–16k.

## Modifications

- `trtllm_mla_backend.py`
  - `init_forward_metadata` finds the decode tail once per forward from `extend_seq_lens_cpu` /
    `extend_prefix_lens_cpu` (no device sync), using the same trailing-one-token rule as #43238 plus a non-empty
    cached prefix. The result goes in a new `TRTLLMMLAMixedDecodeTail` (`msgspec.Struct`) on the prefill metadata,
    with the tail's page table built once for every MLA layer.
  - `forward_mixed_decode_tail` runs the existing `_run_decode_kernel` on the tail rows. The query is built and cast
    exactly as in `forward_decode`, so fp8 and bf16 KV caches are both supported.
  - The causal and prefix passes cover only the prefill requests when the caller passes just their rows. Callers
    that pass every row (other models) get the stock behaviour unchanged.
  - The feature is enabled in `__init__` for `trtllm-gen` without DCP. Subclasses that swap the decode kernel or own
    prefill Q/K/V preparation (`cutedsl_mla`) keep the stock path.
- `forward_mha.py`: `forward_normal_chunked_kv_core` is split into the existing chunked-KV attention
  (`_chunked_kv_attn_mha`, unchanged logic) and a mixed path. The mixed path runs that attention on the prefill rows,
  then serves the tail as `q_nope · W_UK → MLA decode → · W_UV`. Gates: not DSA, bf16 `w_kc`/`w_vc`, no deep-gemm
  bmm, no `kv_b_proj` LoRA, and the query not padded past the batch's real tokens (DP attention).
- `forward_batch_deepseek_mha_mixin.py`: `prepare_chunked_prefix_cache_info(num_reqs=...)` builds the prefix-chunk
  tables for the leading requests only. `prefix_chunk_len` is still sized by the whole batch, so the prefill rows see
  exactly the chunk boundaries they saw before. This matters because the chunk merge is boundary-sensitive (#40903).
- Unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_trtllm_mla_mixed_decode_tail.py`:
  - tail detection;
  - the request range of the causal and prefix passes;
  - the decode-tail kernel call against a PyTorch reference for fp8 and bf16 KV (SM100).

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (real weights) on 1× B200. It has the same per-GPU MLA geometry as DeepSeek-V3 at TP8: 16
heads, kv_lora 512, rope 64. Flags: `--attention-backend trtllm_mla --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --enable-mixed-chunk
--chunked-prefill-size 16384`. Main = nightly `c10e0e17`; release = v0.5.22.

| config | eval | main (before) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.5.22, default flags | GSM8K (`sgl-eval`, 1319) | 56.1% | 56.4% |
| v0.5.22, default flags | MMLU (`sgl-eval`, 2000) | 34.7% | 35.4% |
| v0.5.22, `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph`, 2 runs | 32-shot GSM8K (~6.6k-token prompts, greedy) | 66.7 / 66.0% | 67.6 / 66.6% |
| v0.5.22, bf16 KV, `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` | 32-shot GSM8K | 68.6% | 69.2% |
| main, `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` | 32-shot GSM8K | 66.7% | 67.9% |

- **Why the 32-shot eval exists:** short-prompt evals barely exercise this change, because their extend batches fit
  the prefill CUDA graph. The 32-shot GSM8K uses long prompts so that mixed batches take the changed path.
  Instrumented runs confirmed the new path executes during it.
- **Not bitwise-identical:** the decode rows now go through the decode kernel instead of chunked MHA. On the 32-shot
  run, two stock runs give identical greedy text for 8.6% of prompts and the same final answer for 65.3%. Stock vs
  this PR gives 8.9% and 68.8%. So the PR adds no divergence beyond the engine's own batch-composition
  nondeterminism. The unit test bounds the kernel-level difference against an fp32 reference.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same model and GPU; `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids --tokenize-prompt`. W2 = 128 × 8k → 256, all at once.
W3 = 96 × 16k → 512 arriving at 2 req/s, max concurrency 64.

| config | metric | before | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.5.22, default flags | W2 TPOT | 79.2 ms | 30.5 ms | −61% |
| | W2 output tok/s | 1000 | 2295 | +129% |
| | W3 TPOT | 76.3 ms | 22.0 ms | −71% |
| | W3 output tok/s | 603 | 913 | +51% |
| v0.5.22, `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` (2 runs) | W2 TPOT | 81.3 / 79.5 ms | 30.7 / 30.7 ms | −62% |
| | W3 TPOT | 16.8 / 16.6 ms | 7.9 / 8.0 ms | −52% |
| | W3 mean TTFT | 988 / 989 ms | 351 / 367 ms | −63% |
| v0.5.22, bf16 KV | W2 / W3 TPOT | 70.2 / 16.3 ms | 33.5 / 9.1 ms | −52% / −44% |
| main | W2 / W3 TPOT | 80.6 / 16.8 ms | 30.6 / 7.9 ms | −62% / −53% |
| v0.5.22, **without** `--enable-mixed-chunk` | W2 / W3 TPOT | 30.5 / 7.56 ms | 30.7 / 7.63 ms | no-op |

**Larger-model motivation (speed only).** These are from a truncated Kimi-K3: 48 of 93 layers, 12 of them MLA,
**dummy weights**, 8× B200, TP8. W3 TPOT −23%, W2 TPOT −25%, output throughput +24–25%. K3 has 24 MLA layers out of 93
(the rest are linear attention), so read this as a per-MLA-layer effect, not a full-model number.

**Not tested at full scale:** I don't have the hardware to run DeepSeek-V3/R1 or a full K3 with mixed chunks.
Could a reviewer run a DeepSeek-V3 `--enable-mixed-chunk` GSM8K check, or trigger the Blackwell suites?

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell pass on the changed files).
- [x] Unit test added under `test/registered/unit/` (CustomTestCase, `register_cuda_ci(..., runner_config="4-gpu-b200")`, `__main__`); passes on B200 for v0.5.22 and main.
- [x] Accuracy and speed results above.
- [ ] Docs: none needed (no new flags).

+    def _plan_mixed_decode_tail(
+        self, forward_batch: ForwardBatch
+    ) -> Optional[TRTLLMMLAMixedDecodeTail]:
+        """Find the decode tail from host-side lengths (no device sync) and
+        build its page table once per forward for every MLA layer."""
+        if forward_batch.spec_info is not None:
+            return None
+        extend_lens = forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu
+        prefix_lens = forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens_cpu

+            extend_seq_lens=extend_lens, extend_prefix_lens=prefix_lens

+        if num_prefill_reqs is None:
+            return None

+        # Build the page table over the whole batch and keep the tail rows: a
+        # translated plan's table is laid out from the batch's first request.
+        max_seq_len = max(p + e for p, e in zip(prefix_lens, extend_lens))
+        block_kv_indices = self._create_block_kv_indices(
+            plan=forward_batch.kv_loc_plan,
+            batch_size=forward_batch.batch_size,
+            max_blocks=self._calc_padded_blocks(max_seq_len),
+            req_pool_indices=forward_batch.req_pool_indices,
+            seq_lens=forward_batch.seq_lens,
+            device=forward_batch.seq_lens.device,
+        )
+        return TRTLLMMLAMixedDecodeTail(
+            num_prefill_reqs=num_prefill_reqs,
+            num_prefill_tokens=sum(extend_lens[:num_prefill_reqs]),
+            block_kv_indices=block_kv_indices[num_prefill_reqs:],
+            seq_lens_k=forward_batch.seq_lens[num_prefill_reqs:].to(torch.int32),
+            max_seq_len_k=max(prefix_lens[num_prefill_reqs:]) + 1,
+        )

+        """The current extend batch's decode tail, or None if it has none."""
+        metadata = self.forward_prefill_metadata

+        self,
+        *,
+        q_nope_out: torch.Tensor,
+        q_rope: torch.Tensor,
+        layer: RadixAttention,
+        decode_tail: TRTLLMMLAMixedDecodeTail,

+
+        q_nope_out [n, H, kv_lora_rank] is the query already multiplied by
+        W_UK and q_rope [n, H, qk_rope_head_dim] is post-RoPE; their KV is
+        already in the cache. Returns the latent output [n, H, kv_lora_rank].
+        """

+        query = concat_mla_absorb_q_general(q_nope_out, q_rope).to(self.data_type)
+        k_cache = self.token_to_kv_pool.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id)
+        raw_out = self._run_decode_kernel(
+            query=query.unsqueeze(1),
+            kv_cache=paged_row_view(k_cache, self.page_size).unsqueeze(1),
+            block_tables=decode_tail.block_kv_indices,
+            seq_lens=decode_tail.seq_lens_k,
+            max_seq_len=decode_tail.max_seq_len_k,
+            layer=layer,
+        )
+        return raw_out.view(-1, layer.tp_q_head_num, self.kv_lora_rank)

+            return forward_batch.batch_size, metadata.cum_seq_lens, metadata.seq_lens
+        num_reqs = decode_tail.num_prefill_reqs
+        return (
+            num_reqs,
+            metadata.cum_seq_lens[: num_reqs + 1],
+            metadata.seq_lens[:num_reqs],
+        )

+"""trtllm_mla serves the decode tail of a mixed extend batch with the decode kernel.
+
+With --enable-mixed-chunk, a prefill chunk carries the running requests' decode
+tokens at its end, and the batch runs as EXTEND. trtllm_mla used to attend
+those one-token rows through the chunked-prefix MHA path, re-reading each
+request's whole context per prefix chunk. The backend now finds that tail once
+per forward (from host-side lengths, without a device sync), restricts the
+causal and prefix passes to the prefill requests, and hands the tail to the
+absorbed MLA decode kernel.
+
+Covered here:
+- which trailing requests count as the decode tail;
+- the request range the causal / prefix passes cover;
+- the decode-tail kernel call against a PyTorch reference, for fp8 and bf16 KV
+  (Blackwell only: the kernel is trtllm-gen).
+
+    python3 test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_trtllm_mla_mixed_decode_tail.py
+"""
+
+import math
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.trtllm_mla_backend import (
+    TRTLLMMLABackend,
+    TRTLLMMLAMixedDecodeTail,
+    TRTLLMMLAPrefillMetadata,
+    find_mixed_decode_tail_start,
+    make_persistent_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_flashinfer_available
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+KV_LORA_RANK = 512
+QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM = 64
+QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM = 128
+PAGE_SIZE = 64
+
+
+def _is_sm100() -> bool:
+    return (
+        torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] == 10
+        and is_flashinfer_available()
+    )
+
+
+class TestFindMixedDecodeTailStart(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_cases(self):
+        cases = [
+            # (extend lens, prefix lens, expected start)
+            ([4096, 1, 1, 1], [0, 900, 17, 4000], 1),  # one prefill chunk + 3 decodes
+            ([2048, 300, 1, 1], [0, 512, 64, 64], 2),  # two prefill requests
+            ([4096, 1], [8192, 100], 1),  # prefill with its own cached prefix
+            ([4096, 2048], [0, 0], None),  # pure prefill
+            ([1, 1, 1], [10, 20, 30], None),  # decode-shaped only: no prefill part
+            ([4096, 1], [0, 0], None),  # trailing 1-token prompt (no cached prefix)
+            ([4096, 1, 1], [0, 0, 50], 2),  # the tail stops at the 1-token prompt
+            ([1, 4096], [50, 0], None),  # a 1-token extend that is not trailing
+        ]
+        for extend_lens, prefix_lens, expected in cases:
+            with self.subTest(extend_lens=extend_lens, prefix_lens=prefix_lens):
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    find_mixed_decode_tail_start(
+                        extend_seq_lens=extend_lens, extend_prefix_lens=prefix_lens
+                    ),
+                    expected,
+                )
+

+class TestForwardMixedDecodeTail(CustomTestCase):
+    """forward_mixed_decode_tail = absorbed MLA attention of each tail row over
+    its cached latent KV, through the paged block table."""
+
+    NUM_HEADS = 16
+    SEQ_LENS = [1, 63, 64, 65, 700, 2049]
+
+    def _run(self, kv_dtype: torch.dtype, atol: float):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        device = torch.device("cuda")
+        num_reqs = len(self.SEQ_LENS)
+        kv_dim = KV_LORA_RANK + QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM
+
+        backend = TRTLLMMLABackend.__new__(TRTLLMMLABackend)
+        backend.backend = "trtllm-gen"
+        backend.data_type = kv_dtype
+        backend.page_size = PAGE_SIZE
+        backend.kv_lora_rank = KV_LORA_RANK
+        backend.qk_nope_head_dim = QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM
+        backend.qk_rope_head_dim = QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM
+        backend.workspace_buffer = torch.zeros(
+            128 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.int8, device=device
+        )
+        backend._multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer = (
+            make_persistent_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer(
+                device, self.NUM_HEADS, max_batch_size=num_reqs
+            )
+        )
+
+        # Each request gets its own shuffled pages of one shared latent cache.
+        pages_per_req = [math.ceil(n / PAGE_SIZE) for n in self.SEQ_LENS]
+        page_ids = torch.randperm(sum(pages_per_req) + 3, device=device)[
+            : sum(pages_per_req)
+        ]
+        max_blocks = backend._calc_padded_blocks(max(self.SEQ_LENS))
+        block_table = torch.full(
+            (num_reqs, max_blocks), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+        offset = 0
+        for i, n in enumerate(pages_per_req):
+            block_table[i, :n] = page_ids[offset : offset + n]
+            offset += n
+        num_slots = (sum(pages_per_req) + 3) * PAGE_SIZE
+        kv_cache = (torch.randn(num_slots, 1, kv_dim, device=device) * 0.5).to(kv_dtype)
+        backend.token_to_kv_pool = SimpleNamespace(
+            get_key_buffer=lambda layer_id: kv_cache
+        )
+
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(
+            layer_id=0,
+            tp_q_head_num=self.NUM_HEADS,
+            scaling=(QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM + QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM) ** -0.5,
+            k_scale_float=None,
+        )
+        q_nope_out = torch.randn(
+            num_reqs, self.NUM_HEADS, KV_LORA_RANK, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        q_rope = torch.randn(
+            num_reqs,
+            self.NUM_HEADS,
+            QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM,
+            device=device,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+        decode_tail = TRTLLMMLAMixedDecodeTail(
+            num_prefill_reqs=1,
+            num_prefill_tokens=128,
+            block_kv_indices=block_table,
+            seq_lens_k=torch.tensor(self.SEQ_LENS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+            max_seq_len_k=max(self.SEQ_LENS),
+        )
+
+        with get_parallel().override(dcp_enabled=False):
+            out = backend.forward_mixed_decode_tail(
+                q_nope_out=q_nope_out,
+                q_rope=q_rope,
+                layer=layer,
+                decode_tail=decode_tail,
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (num_reqs, self.NUM_HEADS, KV_LORA_RANK))
+
+        # Reference: softmax(q . [c, k_pe]) . c over each request's tokens, with
+        # the query rounded to the KV dtype as the kernel receives it.
+        query = torch.cat([q_nope_out, q_rope], dim=-1).to(kv_dtype).float()
+        pages = kv_cache.float().view(-1, PAGE_SIZE, kv_dim)
+        for i, n in enumerate(self.SEQ_LENS):
+            kv = pages[block_table[i, : pages_per_req[i]].long()].reshape(-1, kv_dim)
+            kv = kv[:n]
+            scores = query[i] @ kv.T * layer.scaling
+            ref = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1) @ kv[:, :KV_LORA_RANK]
+            torch.testing.assert_close(out[i].float(), ref, atol=atol, rtol=0.05)
+
+    def test_fp8_kv(self):
+        self._run(torch.float8_e4m3fn, atol=3e-2)
+
+    def test_bf16_kv(self):
+        self._run(torch.bfloat16, atol=1e-2)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
